AssignmentRecipient.Definition: The variable, field, or location that receives the value of an assignment.

Attribute.Definition: Attributes add extra information (metadata) to code elements like classes, methods, or properties. Attributes are often used to control behavior or provide instructions to tools and frameworks.

BaseType.Definition: A base type specifies a type that another type inherits from or implements. It defines a parent relationship in the type hierarchy.

CatchExceptionType.Definition: An exception type represents the kind of error that can be thrown or caught. It identifies what went wrong during program execution.

ConditionValue.Definition: A boolean value that will determine if the following code should be executed or skipped.

EventFieldType.Definition: An event field type defines the delegate type used by an event. It determines the shape of the methods that can handle the event.

ForEachLoopCollection.Definition: The collection being iterated over in a {c:color-purple keyword}foreach{/c} loop. The loop retrieves the next element from this collection each iteration.

GenericTypeParameter.Definition: This identifier is a placeholder that will be replaced by a generic type argument. This allows a generic class or method to have one implementation that works for multiple data types.

LockTarget.Definition: The variable that a {c:color-blue keyword}lock{/c} statement uses to control access to the protected code block. Only one execution thread can hold the lock on this target at a time.

ParameterLabel.Definition: A parameter label names an argument when calling a method. It improves readability by making it clear which parameter a value is assigned to.

TargetMember.Definition: The member name token that identifies the property, field, method, or event being accessed on an instance or type.

TernaryCondition.Definition: The boolean value that determines whether the {c:bold}true{/c} or {c:bold}false{/c} expression is returned.

TupleElementName.Definition: A tuple element name gives a readable name to a value inside a tuple. It makes tuple values easier to understand and access.

Type.Definition: The name of a type imported by the using directive.

WithExpressionSource.Definition: The existing value that a {c:color-blue keyword}with{/c} expression copies before applying the specified changes. It provides the starting state for the new value.

NamespaceAliasDeclaration.Definition: An alias name that represents a {c:color-blue keyword}namespace{/c}. It allows shorter or alternative naming when referencing types within that namespace.

TypeAliasDeclaration.Definition: An alias name that represents a specific type. It provides an alternate name for a type, including generic or fully qualified types.

Invocation.Definition: An identifier that when invoked, transfers the execution to the identifier's definition. Execution is transfered back when the invocation expression is completed.

LocalDeclaration.Definition: The identifier for a variable, constant, or local function inside a method, accessor, or block. This identifier can be referenced only within the enclosing scope in which it is defined.

MemberDeclaration.Definition: The identifier for a type member (method, property, field, event, constructor, operator). Where this identifier can be referenced from is determined by the its {c:bold}access modifier{/c}.

ParameterDeclaration.Definition: The identifier for a value that needs to be passed to a method, constructor, or lambda function. This identifier can be referenced only within the body of the member or expression in which it is defined.

AliasQualifier.Definition: An alias qualifier refers to an alias used to access a type or namespace. It helps distinguish which aliased name is being used.

CollectionInstanceQualifer.Definition: The identifier of a collection being used to access an element inside the collection.

ImplicitInstanceQualifier.Definition: The identifier of an object instance being used to access an element of that instance.

InstanceQualifier.Definition: The identifier of an object instance being used to access an element of that instance.

NamespaceQualifier.Definition: A segment of a fully qualified {c:color-blue keyword}namespace{/c}.

TypeDeclaration.Definition: The identifier for a {c:color-blue keyword}class{/c}, {c:color-blue keyword}struct{/c}, {c:color-blue keyword}record{/c}, {c:color-blue keyword}enum{/c}, or {c:color-blue keyword}interface{/c}. The elements defined inside this type are the type members. This identifier can be used to access the members inside.

GroupContinuationRangeVariable.Definition: A group continuation range variable represents a variable introduced after a group operation in a query. It allows the grouped results to be queried further.

GroupElement.Definition: The value or that a {c:color-blue keyword}group{/c} clause places into each resulting group. Each item in the final group comes from this element expression.

JoinIntoRangeVariable.Definition: A join-into range variable represents the result of a join operation in a query. It stores the grouped matches from the join.

JoinRangeVariable.Definition: A join range variable represents a variable used during a join operation in a query. It holds values being compared between data sources.

JoinSource.Definition: A join source represents the data source being joined in a query. It provides the values used for matching during the join.

LetVariable.Definition: A let variable stores the result of an expression inside a query. It helps simplify complex expressions and reuse computed values.

QuerySource.Definition: A query source represents the data being queried in a LINQ expression. It is the starting point for the query.

QueryVariableReference.Definition: A query variable reference refers to a variable used within a query expression. It accesses values introduced earlier in the query.

RangeVariable.Definition: A range variable represents a variable that ranges over elements in a data source. It is used to refer to each element in a query.
